explanation_text: [latex]x(t)=e^{At}X(0)+\int_{0}^{t}e^{A(t-\tau) }BU(\tau )d\tau [/latex] [latex]\because \;\; X(0)=0[/latex]  (as given) [latex]\therefore \;\; x(t)=0+\int_{0}^{t}\begin{bmatrix} e^{2(t-\tau )} &0 \\ 0 & e^{4(t-\tau )} \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 1 \end{bmatrix}\delta (t)dt [/latex] [latex]\;\;=\int_{0}^{t}\begin{bmatrix} e^{2(t-\tau )}\\ e^{2(t-\tau )} \end{bmatrix}\delta (t)dt [/latex] [latex]\;\;=\begin{bmatrix} e^{2t}\\ e^{4t} \end{bmatrix} [/latex] Output  [latex]y(t)=\begin{bmatrix} 4 &0 \end{bmatrix}x(t) [/latex] [latex]\;\;=\begin{bmatrix} 4 &0 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} e^{2t}\\ e^{4t} \end{bmatrix} [/latex] Hence, [latex]y(t)=4e^{2t}[/latex]
explanation_html:
[latex]x(t)=e^{At}X(0)+\int_{0}^{t}e^{A(t-\tau) }BU(\tau )d\tau [/latex]
[latex]\because \;\; X(0)=0[/latex] (as given)
[latex]\therefore \;\; x(t)=0+\int_{0}^{t}\begin{bmatrix} e^{2(t-\tau )} &0 \\ 0 & e^{4(t-\tau )} \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 1 \end{bmatrix}\delta (t)dt [/latex]
[latex]\;\;=\int_{0}^{t}\begin{bmatrix} e^{2(t-\tau )}\\ e^{2(t-\tau )} \end{bmatrix}\delta (t)dt [/latex]
[latex]\;\;=\begin{bmatrix} e^{2t}\\ e^{4t} \end{bmatrix} [/latex]
Output [latex]y(t)=\begin{bmatrix} 4 &0 \end{bmatrix}x(t) [/latex]
[latex]\;\;=\begin{bmatrix} 4 &0 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} e^{2t}\\ e^{4t} \end{bmatrix} [/latex]
Hence, [latex]y(t)=4e^{2t}[/latex]

The switch S is operated with a switching time period T and a duty ratio D. what is the value of D at the boundary of continuous and
discontinuous conduction of the inductor current [latex]i_L[/latex]?
html: In the chopper circuit shown in figure, the input dc voltage has a constant value [latex]V_{s}[/latex]. The output voltage [latex]V_{o}[/latex] is assumed ripple-free. The switch S is operated with a switching time period T and a duty ratio D. what is the value of D at the boundary of continuous and discontinuous conduction of the inductor current [latex]i_L[/latex]?
subject: Power Electronics - Choppers
explanation_text: As the given chopper is buck chopper. [latex]\begin{aligned} V_0&=\alpha V_s\\ \Delta I&=\frac{V_0T_{off}}{L}=\frac{\alpha V_s(1-\alpha )}{Lf}\\ \Delta I&=2I_L=2I_0\\ \Delta I&=2I_0=\frac{\alpha V_s(1-\alpha )}{Lf} \end{aligned}[/latex] [latex]\frac{\Delta L}{2}=I_{L(avg)}=I_{0(avg)}[/latex] this is applicable only at the boundary of continuous and discontinuous [latex]\begin{aligned} L_c &=\frac{\alpha V_s(1-\alpha )}{2I_0f} \\ L_c&=\frac{\alpha V_sR(1-\alpha )}{R2I_0f} \\ (\because & \text{ multiplying and dividing by R}) \\ L_c&=\frac{V_0 R(1-\alpha )}{RI_02f} \\ L_c&= \frac{I_0R(1-\alpha )}{I_02f}\\ L_c&=\frac{R(1-\alpha )}{2f} \\ \therefore &= \text{ Boundary value of duty cycle is,}\\ \frac{2fL}{R}&=1-\alpha \\ \alpha &= 1-\frac{2fL}{R}=1-\frac{2L}{RT} \end{aligned}[/latex]
explanation_html:
As the given chopper is buck chopper.
[latex]\begin{aligned} V_0&=\alpha V_s\\ \Delta I&=\frac{V_0T_{off}}{L}=\frac{\alpha V_s(1-\alpha )}{Lf}\\ \Delta I&=2I_L=2I_0\\ \Delta I&=2I_0=\frac{\alpha V_s(1-\alpha )}{Lf} \end{aligned}[/latex]

[latex]\frac{\Delta L}{2}=I_{L(avg)}=I_{0(avg)}[/latex]
this is applicable only at the boundary of continuous and discontinuous
[latex]\begin{aligned} L_c &=\frac{\alpha V_s(1-\alpha )}{2I_0f} \\ L_c&=\frac{\alpha V_sR(1-\alpha )}{R2I_0f} \\ (\because & \text{ multiplying and dividing by R}) \\ L_c&=\frac{V_0 R(1-\alpha )}{RI_02f} \\ L_c&= \frac{I_0R(1-\alpha )}{I_02f}\\ L_c&=\frac{R(1-\alpha )}{2f} \\ \therefore &= \text{ Boundary value of duty cycle is,}\\ \frac{2fL}{R}&=1-\alpha \\ \alpha &= 1-\frac{2fL}{R}=1-\frac{2L}{RT} \end{aligned}[/latex]

semiconductor switches of the inverter are operated in such a manner that the
pole voltages [latex]V_{10}[/latex] and [latex]V_{20}[/latex] are as shown in figure. What is the rms value of
the pole-to-pole voltage [latex]V_{12}[/latex]?

The semiconductor switches of the inverter are operated in such a manner that the pole voltages [latex]V_{10}[/latex] and [latex]V_{20}[/latex] are as shown in figure. What is the rms value of the pole-to-pole voltage [latex]V_{12}[/latex]?
subject: Power Electronics - Inverters
explanation_text: [latex]\begin{aligned} V_{12}&=V_{10}-V_{20} \\ V_{rms}&=V_s\sqrt{\frac{\phi }{\pi}} \end{aligned}[/latex]
